Last weekend, after spending a quiet afternoon enjoying a few favourite LPs from my personal collection, I reflected on the parallels between my listening habits and my work at Southern Cross Records. In both cases, details matter — whether it's the warmth of an analogue pressing from the '70s or the precision of a newly cut lacquer. Our latest project, a high-fidelity reissue of a seminal 1973 rock album sourced entirely from the original analogue tapes, tested every aspect of our production process. We coordinated closely with the mastering engineer to preserve the depth and dynamic range of the original mixes, and oversaw pressing at a plant renowned for their meticulous quality control. The result is a record that, I believe, will resonate with collectors who value authenticity as much as I do.
